content:
Apple is making a major change to the way iPhones are purchased this week, launching not only the “Apple Upgrade” leasing programme but also discontinuing the “iPhone Upgrade Program”.

With the iPhone 18 series launching in less than a month, I’m really curious: how are you planning to buy your next iPhone?

Speaking for myself, I’ve been enrolled in the “iPhone Upgrade Program” for several years now, so when it comes time to pre-order a new iPhone this autumn, I have a decision to make.

Apple says members of the “iPhone Upgrade Program” can easily switch to other Apple purchase plans when trading in their device. My tentative plan is to switch directly to the 12-month leasing option under the “Apple Upgrade” programme. For someone like me who upgrades every year, this option fits best both financially and in terms of convenience.

The Apple Card is another popular payment method among iPhone users—tempting, sure, but I don’t want the hassle of having to sell or trade in my phone every year.

Through Apple’s website, you can also buy your device via US carrier instalment plans from AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile. But I have no desire to be tied down by these carrier instalment schemes and all the fine print that comes with them.

Finally, of course, you can pay outright for your next iPhone. Whether it’s cold hard cash, a credit card, points or any other method, it all works. That said, as someone who upgrades every year, I don’t want more than a thousand US dollars sitting tied up in a phone over the course of a year.

What about you? Whether you’re planning to buy the iPhone 18 this autumn or waiting a couple more years, how are you planning to buy your next iPhone? Does the “Apple Upgrade” programme tempt you? Do you prefer to pay cash in one go? Feel free to cast your vote below, and you can also explain your choice in the comments.
